     1	# Rung C3 — Looking at your own deck: the information model, and the two cards that need it
     2	
     3	> Revision 1 (2026-08-27). Prerequisite reading: the "What C2 actually built, and what C3 inherits" section of
     4	> `2026-08-27-rung-c2-observer-triggers.md`, and the "WHAT I WOULD DO DIFFERENTLY" section of
     5	> `2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.codex-code-review.md`, both of which say the same thing: decide the
     6	> visibility model **before** adding any deck target.
     7	
     8	## Context
     9	
    10	Ten of the starter deck's 28 printed ability clauses work. The next ones in line all touch a zone no ability
    11	has touched yet — the **deck** — and the engine cannot currently express them for a reason that is not about
    12	targeting at all.
    13	
    14	`Pending.chooseTargets` carries materialised `CardId`s (`packages/engine/src/state.ts:36`). `viewFor` copies
    15	`state.pending` wholesale to **both** players (`packages/engine/src/view.ts:33`), and `determinise` mints
    16	fresh ids for every hidden card and then copies the stale pending ids over the top
    17	(`packages/engine/src/determinise.ts:41`). So a deck target today would be simultaneously **orphaned** for the
    18	player choosing (ids that name nothing in their view) and **leaked** to the player not choosing. Neither is a
    19	bug in targeting; both are the absence of a model for *who knows what*.
    20	
    21	## The two cards, and why they are one card
    22	
    23	| | Miner (20-074C) | Reeve (20-105C) |
    24	|---|---|---|
    25	| Trigger | ETB | ETB (printed `EX BURST`) |
    26	| Sees | **reveal** the top 5 — public | **look at** the top 3 — private |
    27	| Takes | 1 **Backup** among them → hand | 1 **card** among them → hand |
    28	| Rest | to the bottom of the deck, in any order | to the bottom of the deck, in any order |
    29	
    30	Structurally identical: *expose N from the top, take one matching a filter, bottom the rest.* They differ only
    31	in **N**, in the **filter**, and in **who is allowed to watch**. That last difference is the whole rung — it is
    32	the smallest pair of cards that forces the private/public distinction to be built properly rather than fudged,
    33	which is exactly why they are the right two to do first.
    34	
    35	As with Noel and Lightning in C1, the printed `EX BURST` tag on Reeve is quoted but not implemented: the
    36	clause fires on a normal cast, which is what `enterField` means. EX Burst itself stays out of scope.
    37	
    38	## Decisions
    39	
    40	| # | Decision | Ruling (and why) |
    41	|---|---|---|
    42	| C3-1 | **Knowledge is per player, and lives in the view's deck** | `FieldView.deckCount: number` becomes `FieldView.deck: readonly (CardId \| null)[]` — one slot per card, non-null **only** where that viewer legitimately knows what is there. The count is `deck.length`, so nothing is lost. This is the minimal representation that can express "I know my top 3 but not my fourth", which is precisely what Reeve creates. |
    43	| C3-2 | **`determinise` pins what is known and samples the rest** | Non-null slots keep their id and code and are removed from the unseen multiset before shuffling, exactly as field and hand cards already are (`determinise.ts:38`). Everything else is sampled as today. Without this, an AI that looked at its own top 3 would re-randomise them the instant it tried to think about them — the search would be reasoning about a deck it had just been told it did not have. |
    44	| C3-3 | **`viewFor` redacts pending candidates the viewer cannot see** | A `chooseTargets` whose candidates include hidden cards is filtered to those visible **to that viewer**, and carries `hidden: number` for the remainder. The opponent of a Reeve therefore sees "choosing 1 of 3 cards" and no identities. Redaction happens at the view boundary, not at the prompt, because the view boundary is the only place that knows who is asking. |
    45	| C3-4 | **A private choice by the OPPONENT must key on what was observed, not on what was sampled** | In ISMCTS, an opponent's private deck choice is re-sampled every determinisation. Keyed by card identity, one real decision would shatter into dozens of tree nodes that the searcher can never tell apart in play — and each would be conditioned on information the searcher does not have. Action keys for a non-root player's private choice collapse to the observable form (`take 1 of N from deck`). This is the D2 review's warning that "Reeve's private look invalidates the search's assumption that every action becomes public", answered. |
    46	| C3-5 | **`reveal` and `look at` are one primitive with a visibility flag** | `lookAt { count, visibility: 'public' \| 'private', filter, take }`. Public grants the knowledge to both players, private only to the controller. Building these as two effects would duplicate the ordering, filtering and bottoming logic to express a difference of one field. |
    47	| C3-6 | **MVP0-SIMPLIFICATION: "in any order" becomes a fixed order** | The rest go to the bottom in their revealed order; the player is not asked to arrange them. Asking would add a permutation decision (4 cards = 24 orderings) to every Miner, for cards going to the **bottom of a 40+ card deck**, which in a game this length will almost never be drawn. Marked `MVP0-SIMPLIFICATION` at the site with this reasoning, and listed in the README's deviations. |
    48	| C3-7 | Not in scope | **Hugh Yurg** (searches the *whole* deck, and *plays* the card onto the field rather than taking it to hand — that needs a put-into-play-without-paying effect); **Cloud's Attack-Phase clause** (needs attack entry split into preparation + continuation); EX Burst; Sphene; the "in any order" prompt. |
    49	
    50	## What could go wrong, in the order it will bite
    51	
    52	- **The knowledge model leaks the other way.** The interesting failure is not "the opponent saw my card" but
    53	  "the AI saw its own deck when it should not have". `determinise` is the AI's only window onto hidden state,
    54	  and it is *supposed* to invent cards. Pinning slots is a deliberate hole in that invention, so the pin must
    55	  be driven by the view — never by ground truth. A test that determinises from a view and asserts that
    56	  **only** the pinned slots are stable is the guard.
    57	- **`deckCount` → `deck` touches every view consumer.** Cheap but wide; the compiler finds them all.
    58	- **The AI has no reason to value knowledge.** `evaluate` scores material and tempo; knowing the top 3 of your
    59	  deck scores zero. Reeve and Miner will be played for their bodies and their card, which is *most* of their
    60	  value — but the ordering choice among revealed cards will be made by whatever the search's tie-break
    61	  happens to be. Say so rather than claim the AI plays them well.
    62	
    63	## Acceptance criteria
    64	
    65	- **C3-A1** Miner's ETB reveals the top 5 publicly, adds a chosen **Backup** among them to hand, and bottoms
    66	  the rest; if there is no Backup among the five, the reveal still happens and nothing is added.
    67	- **C3-A2** Reeve's ETB shows the top 3 **to its controller only**, adds a chosen card to hand, bottoms the
    68	  rest. A view built for the opponent contains **none** of the three identities, and its pending reports
    69	  `hidden: 3`.
    70	- **C3-A3 (the determinisation guard)** From a view in which the controller knows its top 3, `determinise`
    71	  reproduces those three ids and codes **exactly**, and samples every other deck slot. From the opponent's
    72	  view of the same state, all three are sampled.
    73	- **C3-A4 (no leak through the search)** Two determinisations of the same opponent-private choice produce the
    74	  **same** action key, and that key does not name a card.
    75	- **C3-A5** A deck with fewer cards than the reveal count reveals what is there and does not throw; an empty
    76	  deck is a no-op, not a loss (deck-out is checked by its own rule process).
    77	- **C3-A6** `ABILITY_CLAUSES` for both cards drops by one clause each, the amber "not implemented" warning
    78	  stops naming the implemented clause, and the marker audit still passes.
    79	- **C3-A7** `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm --filter @fftcg/web build` green; fuzzer
    80	  200/200 with zero failures; ISMCTS still beats greedy over a mirrored run (no strength claim beyond "not
    81	  worse" — see below).
    82	
    83	## What this rung will NOT claim
    84	
    85	It will not claim the AI plays these cards *well*. The honest statement after C1/C2/D1 is that a win-rate gate
    86	cannot see the defects that matter, and a two-card ability addition is far below the noise floor of a 120-game
    87	mirrored run. The strength gate here is a **guard against regression**, not evidence of improvement, and the
    88	report will say so.

Capture controller from the field array and owner from `state.cards[id].owner`. |
    25	| C2-3 | One trigger occurrence per **(watcher, clause, matching transition)** | **Not** once per batch.    251	     4	> mine. The review is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.codex-review.md`.

   253	     6	## Context
   254	     7	
   255	     8	D1 is merged (`b22be0f`): headless SO-ISMCTS beats `GreedyAgent` **90.0 %** over 120 mirrored games at
   256	     9	~254 ms/decision. **The browser still plays `GreedyAgent`** — D1 was headless by design, because 254 ms of
   257	    10	synchronous search would freeze the board mid-turn.
   258	    11	
   259	    12	D2 is the wiring only. The search core does not change: `searchIsmcts(input): SearchResult` is already

   261	    14	
   262	    15	## Architecture: three layers, because the races must be testable
   263	    16	
   264	    17	Revision 1 put worker lifecycle, pacing, retries, fallback and stale-result handling into `useGame`'s AI
   265	    18	`useEffect`. That hook already owns state, pacing, mutation and the agent loop; adding this to it would make
   266	    19	every D2-specific race a matter of React timing folklore rather than a test.
   267	    20	
   268	    21	1. **`protocol.ts`** — discriminated message types and the pure `respond(init, request)`. Deterministic
   269	    22	   translation only; no lifecycle, no knowledge of what is outstanding.
   270	    23	2. **`worker.ts`** — a thin shell: store init, `try`/`catch`, `postMessage`. Vitest cannot drive a real
   271	    24	   `Worker`, so the shell deliberately contains nothing worth testing.
   272	    25	3. **`SearchCoordinator`** — one worker per mounted hook. Owns generation/request tracking, stable
   273	    26	   per-position seeds, the pacing deadline, the watchdog, termination, and the `GreedyAgent` fallback.

   275	    28	
   276	    29	`useGame` then does what it already does: capture a state, ask for a command, re-check legality against that
   277	    30	exact state, narrate, commit.
   278	    31	
   279	    32	## Decisions
   280	    33	
   281	    34	| # | Decision | Ruling (and why) |
   282	    35	|---|---|---|
   283	    36	| D2-1 | A **discriminated wire contract** | `type: 'init' \| 'search' \| 'result' \| 'error'`. Init carries the two declared deck lists **and the stable search configuration** (`rolloutCommandCap`, `explorationC` — `SearchInput` requires them and revision 1's request listed only seed and iterations). Errors carry their `requestId`, or `null` for an init failure, and post **plain strings, never `Error` objects**. |
   284	    37	| D2-2 | **Decks and config at init; the view per request** | `PlayerView` carries `defs` by design and the UI needs them; the search already clones a state containing the same definitions once per determinisation, so one 18-card catalogue per request is not the dominant cost. Revision 1 called this "measured as negligible" — **it was not measured**; D2-A2 now reports the actual serialized size and posting duration, and `Omit<PlayerView,'defs'>` is revisited only if the catalogue materially grows. |
   285	    38	| D2-3 | **Search seeds are stable per game POSITION** | Derived from `(gameSeed, committedAiDecisionIndex)`, incremented **only when an AI command successfully commits**. Never from `requestId`. A seed advanced when the effect *posts* is consumed again by StrictMode's double-invoke, by a retry, by a stale request and by worker replacement — so dev and prod would choose different moves from the same board, which is the worst kind of "works on my machine". |
   286	    39	| D2-4 | **A result is accepted only under all four conditions** | `mounted && activeRequestId === result.requestId && stateRef.current === requestedState && actingPlayer(requestedState) === AI`. Then clear the active id *before* applying, re-check the command against `legalCommands(requestedState, AI)`, and commit from that same captured state. Restart, any external commit, effect cleanup and unmount must **synchronously** invalidate the active id; unmount must also terminate the worker. Note the non-obvious racer: **concede is legal even when the human is not the acting player**, so a human `choose()` really can commit mid-AI-turn. |
   287	    40	| D2-5 | **Pacing is a deadline, not an added delay** | `notBefore = startedAt + AI_STEP_MS`; when the result arrives, schedule at `Math.max(0, notBefore - performance.now())`. A fast search still waits out the 600 ms; a 750 ms search applies immediately, having already shown 750 ms of thinking. Revision 1's "apply at `max(elapsed, AI_STEP_MS)`" was ambiguous enough to be implemented as an *extra* 600 ms. |
   288	    41	| D2-6 | **Fall back to `GreedyAgent`, detect every way it can fail, and say so** | Greedy, not reduced-iteration main-thread ISMCTS: the latter is still a synchronous search with variable rollout cost, which gives up the one guarantee this rung exists for. Detection must cover **missing `Worker`, constructor failure, synchronous `postMessage` clone failure, `error`, `messageerror`, a typed `WorkerError`, and a worker that is killed or hangs and simply never replies** — the last needs a startup and per-request **watchdog**, because nothing correlated ever arrives. On failure: invalidate the request, terminate the worker, switch to Greedy **permanently for that game**, append **one** visible log warning, and play Greedy against the current state under the same pacing deadline. |
   289	    42	| D2-7 | **The iteration budget is measured in the browser** | D1's 200 was an implementation default, never calibrated. Measure, choose, and record the number with the machine and browser it came from. If the browser budget lands well below 200, **the opponent a human faces is weaker than the one D1 measured**, and that gets said. |
   290	    43	| D2-8 | Not in scope | Any change to the search, its keys or its evaluation; a worker pool or parallel search; C3's ability clauses. |
   291	    44	
   292	    45	## Build hazard: partly cleared, and the rest is an acceptance gate
   293	    46	
   294	    47	A throwaway worker importing `searchIsmcts` resolved the raw-TypeScript workspace packages in both modes:
   295	    48	dev logged `worker sees searchIsmcts as: function`, and `vite build` emitted a **52 kB worker chunk**
   296	    49	separate from the 275 kB app chunk. `new Worker(new URL(…, import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })` is Vite's
   297	    50	supported static form, and linked monorepo packages exporting ESM are treated as source.
   298	    51	
   299	    52	**That proves the chunk is emitted, not that it loads and runs when served** — revision 1 claimed the hazard
   300	    53	"cleared", which was too strong. `server.fs.allow` is dev-only; production takes a different bundler path,
   301	    54	and hashed asset loading, MIME and base-path failures all live there. Hence D2-A7 below.
   302	    55	
   303	    56	## Acceptance criteria
   304	    57	
   305	    58	- **D2-A1** The browser plays a **full game to a result** against ISMCTS, end to end, no uncaught errors.
   306	    59	- **D2-A2 (honest non-blocking measurement)** On a **production preview**, over N AI decisions: mark
   307	    60	  request-post, response and commit; observe **`longtask` entries** (any reported entry is ≥ 50 ms by
   308	    61	  definition); record the **maximum `requestAnimationFrame` gap**; inject a harmless test button and record
   309	    62	  **input-to-handler** while a search is active. Report browser, machine, iterations, sample count, max long
   310	    63	  task, max frame gap, max input delay, and worker round-trip p50/p95 — plus the request's serialized size
   311	    64	  and posting duration (D2-2). *"No main-thread task ≥ 50 ms during N AI searches"* is a result;
   312	    65	  *"well under 600 ms"* is not, and was revision 1's wording.
   313	    66	- **D2-A3 (determinism across the boundary)** The same `(view, seed, iterations, caps)` through `respond`
   314	    67	  returns exactly the command a direct `searchIsmcts` call returns.
   315	    68	- **D2-A4 (staleness, at the right layer)** Tested against the **coordinator**, not `respond`: deferred
   316	    69	  replies delivered after a restart, after a human commit (including concede), after StrictMode cleanup, and
   317	    70	  after unmount must all be dropped, and the worker terminated on unmount.
   318	    71	- **D2-A5 (fallback)** Each detectable failure — no `Worker`, constructor throw, clone failure, `error`,
   319	    72	  `messageerror`, typed error, and a never-replying worker — switches to Greedy, logs **one** warning, and
   320	    73	  still finishes a game.
   321	    74	- **D2-A6** The chosen iteration budget is recorded with the measurement that produced it.
   322	    75	- **D2-A7** `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` **and `pnpm --filter @fftcg/web build`** green, plus
   323	    76	  a **production-preview** browser run that loads the emitted worker asset, completes a real `postMessage`
   324	    77	  round trip, and asserts ISMCTS is actually playing rather than the fallback. Headless gates untouched
   325	    78	  (462 tests, ISMCTS 90.0 % vs greedy, strict fuzzer 0 failures).
   326	    79	
   327	    80	## Risks
   328	    81	
   329	    82	- **Staleness is intermittent by nature**, and it is the reason for the coordinator layer. A late result
   330	    83	  applied to a moved-on board corrupts a game rarely and unreproducibly.
   331	    84	- **The fallback can hide itself.** If the worker silently fails the game keeps working and simply plays
   332	    85	  worse — hence one visible warning, and hence D2-A7 asserting ISMCTS rather than merely "a game happened".
   333	    86	- **Seed drift between dev and prod** (D2-3) would be diagnosed as a search bug and is not one.
   334	    87	- **D1's caveats stand**: the iteration budget was never strength-calibrated, and rollouts are ~117× the
   335	    88	  tree cost.
   336	    89	
   337	    90	## Changelog vs revision 1
   338	    91	
   339	    92	- **Three-layer architecture with a `SearchCoordinator`** — revision 1 put lifecycle, retries, watchdog and
   340	    93	  fallback into a `useEffect`, where none of the races could be tested.
   341	    94	- **Staleness moved to the coordinator** with the four-condition acceptance rule (D2-4); revision 1 tested
   342	    95	  it against pure `respond`, which cannot see any of it.
   343	    96	- **Stable per-position seeds** (D2-3) — new; revision 1 left seed allocation undefined.
   344	    97	- **Fallback detection enumerated**, including the watchdog for a worker that never replies (D2-6).
   345	    98	- **D2-A2 replaced with an actual measurement protocol**; the old criterion was unfalsifiable.
   346	    99	- **Production build and preview added to D2-A7**; the dev probe proved emission, not execution.
   347	   100	- **Wire contract completed** — discriminated union, config at init, `requestId` on errors, plain strings.
   348	   101	- **Pacing restated as a deadline** (D2-5).

   350	   103	## Measurement (D2-A2 / D2-A6), taken 2026-08-27
   351	   104	
   352	   105	Production preview (`vite build` + `vite preview`, port 5310), Chromium via Playwright, Apple Silicon
   353	   106	(darwin 25.5.0), default budget **200 iterations**, `rolloutCommandCap` 24, `rolloutApplyCap` 2048.
   354	   107	Three complete games driven end to end; the numbers below are the second and third, where a patched
   355	   108	`Worker` constructor recorded every message.
   356	   109	
   357	   110	| Quantity | Result |
   358	   111	|---|---|
   359	   112	| Worker asset actually served | `GET /assets/worker-DkZKnaJU.js → 200` (hashed production chunk, 52.8 kB) |
   360	   113	| Searches posted / results received / worker errors | **33 / 33 / 0**, then **34 / 34 / 0** |
   361	   114	| Worker round trip | **p50 152 ms, p95 240 ms, max 288 ms** |
   362	   115	| Main-thread `longtask` entries during those searches | **0** (any reported entry would be ≥ 50 ms) |
   363	   116	| Maximum `requestAnimationFrame` gap | **22 ms**, then **19 ms** |
   364	   117	| Input delay, real trusted clicks (Event Timing, n = 12) | **0–1 ms** (`processingStart − startTime`) |
   365	   118	| Search request serialized size | median **14.2 kB**, max 15.4 kB |
   366	   119	| `postMessage` duration (main-thread cost of posting) | max **0.20 ms** |
   367	   120	| Fallback warnings logged | **none** |
   368	   121	
   369	   122	**Reading the numbers.** The frame gap is the load-bearing one: a 200-iteration search on the main thread
   370	   123	would have shown a rAF gap of at least its own duration, so a max gap of 19–22 ms across whole games is
   371	   124	direct evidence the search never ran there. Zero `longtask` entries says the same thing from the other side.
   372	   125	
   373	   126	The *first* pass at input delay used synthetic `.click()` and reported a flat 0 ms — worthless, because a
   374	   127	programmatic click dispatches synchronously and measures nothing. The table's figure is from real Playwright
   375	   128	input observed through `PerformanceEventTiming`.
   376	   129	
   377	   130	**D2-2 resolved.** Leaving `defs` in the per-request view costs 14.2 kB and **0.20 ms** of main-thread
   378	   131	posting. Revision 1 called this "negligible" without measuring; measured, it is in fact negligible, and
   379	   132	`Omit<PlayerView,'defs'>` stays unnecessary.
   380	   133	
   381	   134	**D2-6 / D2-A7 asserted positively.** Every AI decision in both instrumented games was a completed worker
   382	   135	round trip (33/33, 34/34, zero errors, zero fallback warnings). This is the assertion the spec asked for —
   383	   136	not "no warning appeared", which is only evidence of silence.
   384	   137	
   385	   138	**D2-A6: the budget does not need reducing.** Round trips of p50 152 ms / p95 240 ms bracket D1's headless
   386	   139	~254 ms per decision, so the browser affords the **same 200 iterations D1 measured**. The risk the spec
   387	   140	raised — that the human would face a weaker opponent than the 90.0 % one — did not materialise: the browser
   388	   141	opponent is the D1 opponent. The budget still has not been *strength*-calibrated (D1's caveat stands); what
   389	   142	is now known is that the browser is not the thing forcing it down.

   427	+export interface SearchTransport {
   428	+  post(message: WorkerRequestMessage): void
   429	+  terminate(): void
   430	+}
   431	+
   432	+export interface TransportHandlers {

   440	+export interface Clock {

   443	+  after(ms: number, fn: () => void): () => void

   445	+
   446	+export const realClock: Clock = {

   472	+/**
   473	+ * The search seed for the n-th COMMITTED AI decision of a game. Derived from the position rather than the
   474	+ * request, so StrictMode's double-invoke, a retry, a superseded request and a replaced worker all re-ask the
   475	+ * same question and get the same answer. A seed advanced when a request is *posted* makes development and
   476	+ * production choose different moves from the same board — which reads as a search bug and is not one.

   479	+ * this one number into its three streams itself (spec D-8).

   481	+export function searchSeed(gameSeed: number, decisionIndex: number): number {
   482	+  let h = (gameSeed ^ Math.imul(decisionIndex + 1, 0x9e3779b1)) >>> 0
   483	+  h = Math.imul(h ^ (h >>> 16), 0x85ebca6b) >>> 0
   484	+  h = Math.imul(h ^ (h >>> 13), 0xc2b2ae35) >>> 0
   485	+  return (h ^ (h >>> 16)) >>> 0
   486	+}

   789	+ */

   795	+ */

   797	+  readonly type: 'init'

   800	+  readonly rolloutCommandCap: number

   805	+export interface WorkerSearchRequest {

   807	+  readonly requestId: number
   808	+  readonly view: PlayerView
   809	+  readonly seed: number
   810	+  readonly iterations: number
   811	+}

   815	+  readonly requestId: number

   817	+}

   820	+export interface WorkerErrorMessage {

   822	+  readonly requestId: number | null
   823	+  readonly message: string

   906	+}

  1140	+const actorOf = (state: GameState): PlayerId | null => (state.result ? null : (state.pending?.player ?? state.priority))
  1141	+
  1142	+/** Fast-forward a real game to a position the AI actually owns — the only kind the coordinator may be asked for. */
  1143	+function aiToAct(seed: number): GameState {
  1144	+  let state: GameState = createGame({ seed, decks: DECKS, defs: CARD_DEFS })
  1145	+  const agent = new GreedyAgent({ seed, decks: DECKS, depth: 1 })
  1146	+  for (let i = 0; i < 400; i++) {
  1147	+    const p = actorOf(state)
  1148	+    if (p === null) break
  1149	+    if (p === AI) return state
  1150	+    state = apply(state, agent.decide(viewFor(state, p), legalCommands(state, p))).state
  1151	+  }
  1152	+  throw new Error(`seed ${seed} never reached an AI decision`)
  1153	+}
  1154	+
  1155	+function humanToAct(seed: number): GameState {
  1156	+  let state: GameState = createGame({ seed, decks: DECKS, defs: CARD_DEFS })
  1157	+  const agent = new GreedyAgent({ seed, decks: DECKS, depth: 1 })
  1158	+  for (let i = 0; i < 400; i++) {
  1159	+    const p = actorOf(state)
  1160	+    if (p === null) break
  1161	+    if (p === HUMAN) return state
  1162	+    state = apply(state, agent.decide(viewFor(state, p), legalCommands(state, p))).state
  1163	+  }
  1164	+  throw new Error(`seed ${seed} never reached a human decision`)
  1165	+}

  1167	+const EMPTY_DIAGNOSTICS: SearchDiagnostics = {
  1168	+  determinisations: 1, treeApplies: 1, rolloutApplies: 1, evaluations: 1, nodes: 1, maxCommandDepth: 1, rootChildren: [],
  1169	+}
  1170	+
  1171	+/** A worker reply for `state`, carrying a command that really is legal there so nothing downstream is faked. */
  1172	+function resultFor(state: GameState, requestId: number): WorkerResponseMessage {
  1173	+  const command = legalCommands(state, AI)[0]
  1174	+  if (!command) throw new Error('no legal AI command')
  1175	+  const result: SearchResult = { command, diagnostics: EMPTY_DIAGNOSTICS }
  1176	+  return { type: 'result', requestId, result }

  1178	+
  1179	+class FakeClock implements Clock {
  1180	+  private t = 0
  1181	+  private seq = 0
  1182	+  private readonly timers = new Map<number, { at: number; fn: () => void }>()
  1183	+
  1184	+  now(): number { return this.t }
  1185	+
  1186	+  after(ms: number, fn: () => void): () => void {
  1187	+    const id = ++this.seq
  1188	+    this.timers.set(id, { at: this.t + ms, fn })
  1189	+    return () => { this.timers.delete(id) }
  1190	+  }
  1191	+
  1192	+  get armed(): number { return this.timers.size }
  1193	+
  1194	+  advance(ms: number): void {
  1195	+    const target = this.t + ms
  1196	+    for (;;) {
  1197	+      let pickId = -1
  1198	+      let pickAt = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY
  1199	+      for (const [id, timer] of this.timers) {
  1200	+        if (timer.at <= target && (timer.at < pickAt || (timer.at === pickAt && id < pickId))) { pickAt = timer.at; pickId = id }
  1201	+      }
  1202	+      const timer = pickId < 0 ? undefined : this.timers.get(pickId)
  1203	+      if (!timer) break
  1204	+      this.timers.delete(pickId)
  1205	+      this.t = timer.at
  1206	+      timer.fn()
  1207	+    }
  1208	+    this.t = target
  1209	+  }
  1210	+}
  1211	+
  1212	+class FakeTransport implements SearchTransport {
  1213	+  readonly sent: WorkerRequestMessage[] = []
  1214	+  terminations = 0
  1215	+  postThrows: string | null = null
  1216	+  constructor(readonly handlers: TransportHandlers) {}
  1217	+
  1218	+  post(message: WorkerRequestMessage): void {
  1219	+    if (this.postThrows !== null) throw new DOMException(this.postThrows, 'DataCloneError')
  1220	+    this.sent.push(message)
  1221	+  }
  1222	+
  1223	+  terminate(): void { this.terminations++ }
  1224	+
  1225	+  get searches(): WorkerSearchRequest[] {
  1226	+    return this.sent.filter((m): m is WorkerSearchRequest => m.type === 'search')
  1227	+  }
  1228	+}

  1230	+interface Harness {
  1231	+  readonly clock: FakeClock

  1235	+  readonly warnings: string[]
  1236	+  readonly handlers: SearchRequestHandlers
  1237	+  readonly transport: () => FakeTransport
  1238	+  readState(): GameState
  1239	+  setState(state: GameState): void
  1240	+  setCommit(v: boolean): void
  1241	+}

  1243	+function harness(opts: { seed?: number; factory?: SearchTransportFactory; onCreate?: (t: FakeTransport) => void } = {}): Harness {
  1244	+  const clock = new FakeClock()
  1245	+  const transports: FakeTransport[] = []
  1246	+  const delivered: { command: Command; state: GameState }[] = []
  1247	+  const warnings: string[] = []
  1248	+  let current = aiToAct(opts.seed ?? 11)
  1249	+  let commits = true
  1250	+
  1251	+  const handlers: SearchRequestHandlers = {
  1252	+    onCommand: (command, forState) => { delivered.push({ command, state: forState }); return commits },
  1253	+    onWarning: (text) => { warnings.push(text) },
  1254	+  }
  1255	+  const factory: SearchTransportFactory = opts.factory ?? ((h) => {
  1256	+    const t = new FakeTransport(h)
  1257	+    transports.push(t)
  1258	+    opts.onCreate?.(t)
  1259	+    return t
  1260	+  })
  1261	+  const coordinator = new SearchCoordinator({
  1262	+    decks: DECKS,
  1263	+    gameSeed: GAME_SEED,
  1264	+    readState: () => current,
  1265	+    stepMs: STEP_MS,
  1266	+    iterations: 25,
  1267	+    rolloutCommandCap: 8,
  1268	+    explorationC: 1,
  1269	+    watchdogMs: WATCHDOG_MS,
  1270	+    startupWatchdogMs: STARTUP_WATCHDOG_MS,
  1271	+    createTransport: factory,
  1272	+    clock,
  1273	+  })
  1274	+  return {
  1275	+    clock, coordinator, transports, delivered, warnings, handlers,
  1276	+    transport: () => { const t = transports[0]; if (!t) throw new Error('no transport was created'); return t },
  1277	+    readState: () => current,
  1278	+    setState: (s) => { current = s },
  1279	+    setCommit: (v) => { commits = v },
  1280	+  }
  1281	+}

  1283	+/** The whole point of the fallback: whatever went wrong, a command still arrives on the same deadline. */
  1284	+function expectOneWarningAndACommand(h: Harness): void {

  1286	+  h.clock.advance(STEP_MS)

  1289	+  expect(h.warnings[0]).toContain(FALLBACK_WARNING)

  1293	+  expect(legalCommands(only.state, AI).some((c) => c.type === only.command.type)).toBe(true)
  1294	+}

  1826	 # Rung D2 — The search in a Web Worker: the browser gets the strong opponent
  1827	 
  1828	+> Revision 2 (2026-08-27), after a Codex plan-review that found two blockers and corrected two claims of
  1829	+> mine. The review is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.codex-review.md`.
  1830	+
  1831	 ## Context
  1832	 
  1833	 D1 is merged (`b22be0f`): headless SO-ISMCTS beats `GreedyAgent` **90.0 %** over 120 mirrored games at
  1834	 ~254 ms/decision. **The browser still plays `GreedyAgent`** — D1 was headless by design, because 254 ms of
  1835	-synchronous search would block the main thread and freeze the board mid-turn.
  1836	+synchronous search would freeze the board mid-turn.
  1837	+
  1838	+D2 is the wiring only. The search core does not change: `searchIsmcts(input): SearchResult` is already
  1839	+pure, synchronous and structured-cloneable, which is what D1 was told to leave behind.
  1840	+
  1841	+## Architecture: three layers, because the races must be testable
  1842	+
  1843	+Revision 1 put worker lifecycle, pacing, retries, fallback and stale-result handling into `useGame`'s AI
  1844	+`useEffect`. That hook already owns state, pacing, mutation and the agent loop; adding this to it would make
  1845	+every D2-specific race a matter of React timing folklore rather than a test.
  1846	 
  1847	-D2 is the wiring, and only the wiring. The search core does not change: `searchIsmcts(input): SearchResult`
  1848	-is already pure, synchronous and structured-cloneable, which is exactly what D1 was told to leave behind so
  1849	-this rung would not have to rewrite it.
  1850	+1. **`protocol.ts`** — discriminated message types and the pure `respond(init, request)`. Deterministic
  1851	+   translation only; no lifecycle, no knowledge of what is outstanding.
  1852	+2. **`worker.ts`** — a thin shell: store init, `try`/`catch`, `postMessage`. Vitest cannot drive a real
  1853	+   `Worker`, so the shell deliberately contains nothing worth testing.
  1854	+3. **`SearchCoordinator`** — one worker per mounted hook. Owns generation/request tracking, stable
  1855	+   per-position seeds, the pacing deadline, the watchdog, termination, and the `GreedyAgent` fallback.
  1856	+   **This is the layer the D2 tests target**, because this is where every race lives.
  1857	+
  1858	+`useGame` then does what it already does: capture a state, ask for a command, re-check legality against that
  1859	+exact state, narrate, commit.
  1860	 
  1861	 ## Decisions
  1862	 
  1863	 | # | Decision | Ruling (and why) |
  1864	 |---|---|---|
  1865	-| D2-1 | A **typed worker protocol**, not ad-hoc `postMessage` | `WorkerInit` (the two declared deck lists, sent once), `WorkerSearchRequest` (`requestId`, `view`, `seed`, `iterations`), `WorkerSearchResult` (`requestId`, `command`, `diagnostics`) and `WorkerError`. Every one structured-cloneable. Codex's D1 review flagged that the seam *promised* this and did not have it. |
  1866	-| D2-2 | **Decks at init; the view per request** | Decks are what the search needs and the view does not carry. `PlayerView` already carries `defs`, so a request re-sends the 18-card catalogue — measured as negligible against a 600 ms turn, so **it is left alone**. Stripping `defs` and rehydrating in the worker is available if measurement ever says otherwise; doing it now would be optimising a cost nobody has shown. |
  1867	-| D2-3 | **A pure `respond(init, request)` the worker merely wraps** | The same trick that made D1 testable: all protocol logic lives in a plain function, and `worker.ts` is a thin `onmessage` shell. Vitest cannot drive a real `Worker`, so anything inside the shell is untestable — the shell therefore contains nothing worth testing. |
  1868	-| D2-4 | **Requests are generation-checked; stale results are dropped** | `requestId` increases monotonically; the hook ignores any result that is not the one it is waiting for. Restarting a game, or the human acting while the AI thinks, must not have a late result applied to a board that has moved on. This is the defect most likely to be *intermittent* rather than reproducible, so it gets an explicit test rather than an inspection. |
  1869	-| D2-5 | **Search overlaps the pacing delay, never adds to it** | B7 paces the AI at 600 ms so its turn is watchable. Firing the request *then* waiting 600 ms would make every AI move 850 ms. Start the search immediately and apply the result at `max(elapsed, AI_STEP_MS)`, so the search is free until it exceeds the pacing budget. |
  1870	-| D2-6 | **Fall back to `GreedyAgent`, and say so** | If `Worker` is unavailable, the module fails to load, or the worker errors, the game continues with the heuristic agent rather than freezing or silently blocking the main thread. It must be **visible in the log** — an opponent quietly one-tenth as strong is exactly the kind of degradation that goes unnoticed for a rung. |
  1871	-| D2-7 | **The iteration budget is measured in the browser, not inherited** | D1's 200 was an implementation default chosen to be "clearly above greedy without being unusable headless", never calibrated. D2 measures ms/iteration in a real browser and picks a budget for a decision that comfortably fits the pacing window, then records the number and the machine it came from. |
  1872	-| D2-8 | Not in scope | Any change to the search itself, its keys or its evaluation; a worker pool or parallel search; C3's ability clauses. |
  1873	-
  1874	-## Build hazard: cleared before designing around it
  1875	+| D2-1 | A **discriminated wire contract** | `type: 'init' \| 'search' \| 'result' \| 'error'`. Init carries the two declared deck lists **and the stable search configuration** (`rolloutCommandCap`, `explorationC` — `SearchInput` requires them and revision 1's request listed only seed and iterations). Errors carry their `requestId`, or `null` for an init failure, and post **plain strings, never `Error` objects**. |
  1876	+| D2-2 | **Decks and config at init; the view per request** | `PlayerView` carries `defs` by design and the UI needs them; the search already clones a state containing the same definitions once per determinisation, so one 18-card catalogue per request is not the dominant cost. Revision 1 called this "measured as negligible" — **it was not measured**; D2-A2 now reports the actual serialized size and posting duration, and `Omit<PlayerView,'defs'>` is revisited only if the catalogue materially grows. |
  1877	+| D2-3 | **Search seeds are stable per game POSITION** | Derived from `(gameSeed, committedAiDecisionIndex)`, incremented **only when an AI command successfully commits**. Never from `requestId`. A seed advanced when the effect *posts* is consumed again by StrictMode's double-invoke, by a retry, by a stale request and by worker replacement — so dev and prod would choose different moves from the same board, which is the worst kind of "works on my machine". |
  1878	+| D2-4 | **A result is accepted only under all four conditions** | `mounted && activeRequestId === result.requestId && stateRef.current === requestedState && actingPlayer(requestedState) === AI`. Then clear the active id *before* applying, re-check the command against `legalCommands(requestedState, AI)`, and commit from that same captured state. Restart, any external commit, effect cleanup and unmount must **synchronously** invalidate the active id; unmount must also terminate the worker. Note the non-obvious racer: **concede is legal even when the human is not the acting player**, so a human `choose()` really can commit mid-AI-turn. |
  1879	+| D2-5 | **Pacing is a deadline, not an added delay** | `notBefore = startedAt + AI_STEP_MS`; when the result arrives, schedule at `Math.max(0, notBefore - performance.now())`. A fast search still waits out the 600 ms; a 750 ms search applies immediately, having already shown 750 ms of thinking. Revision 1's "apply at `max(elapsed, AI_STEP_MS)`" was ambiguous enough to be implemented as an *extra* 600 ms. |
  1880	+| D2-6 | **Fall back to `GreedyAgent`, detect every way it can fail, and say so** | Greedy, not reduced-iteration main-thread ISMCTS: the latter is still a synchronous search with variable rollout cost, which gives up the one guarantee this rung exists for. Detection must cover **missing `Worker`, constructor failure, synchronous `postMessage` clone failure, `error`, `messageerror`, a typed `WorkerError`, and a worker that is killed or hangs and simply never replies** — the last needs a startup and per-request **watchdog**, because nothing correlated ever arrives. On failure: invalidate the request, terminate the worker, switch to Greedy **permanently for that game**, append **one** visible log warning, and play Greedy against the current state under the same pacing deadline. |
  1881	+| D2-7 | **The iteration budget is measured in the browser** | D1's 200 was an implementation default, never calibrated. Measure, choose, and record the number with the machine and browser it came from. If the browser budget lands well below 200, **the opponent a human faces is weaker than the one D1 measured**, and that gets said. |
  1882	+| D2-8 | Not in scope | Any change to the search, its keys or its evaluation; a worker pool or parallel search; C3's ability clauses. |

  1904	 ## Acceptance criteria
  1905	 
  1906	-- **D2-A1** The browser plays a **full game to a result** against ISMCTS, driven end to end, with no
  1907	-  uncaught errors.
  1908	-- **D2-A2** **The main thread is not blocked.** Measured, not asserted: the longest task during an AI turn
  1909	-  stays well under the pacing window, and the board stays responsive to a click while the AI is thinking.
  1910	-- **D2-A3** **Determinism across the boundary**: the same `(view, seed, iterations)` through `respond`
  1911	-  returns exactly the command a direct `searchIsmcts` call returns. The worker must not be a second,
  1912	-  subtly different agent.
  1913	-- **D2-A4** **Staleness**: a result whose `requestId` is not the outstanding one is dropped. Tested by
  1914	-  driving `respond` out of order, not by hoping the race does not happen.
  1915	-- **D2-A5** **Fallback**: with `Worker` unavailable the game still plays a full game, using `GreedyAgent`,
  1916	-  and the log says which opponent is playing.

  1940	 ## Risks
  1941	 
  1942	-- **Staleness is intermittent by nature.** A late result applied to a moved-on board would corrupt the game
  1943	-  rarely and unreproducibly — the worst failure shape there is. D2-A4 is the mitigation and it must be a
  1944	-  test, not a code reading.
  1945	-- **The fallback can hide itself.** If the worker silently fails, the game keeps working and simply plays
  1946	-  worse. Hence D2-6's requirement that it be visible in the log.
  1947	-- **Vite worker bundling.** `new Worker(new URL('./worker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })` is the
  1948	-  supported form; the workspace packages are raw TypeScript, so the worker bundle must resolve them the same
  1949	-  way the app does. A worker that fails to build is loud; one that builds but silently falls back is not.
  1950	-- **The search is unchanged, so its D1 caveats stand**: the iteration budget was never strength-calibrated,
  1951	-  and rollouts are ~117× the tree cost. If the browser budget lands well below 200 iterations, the opponent
  1952	-  the human faces is weaker than the one D1 measured — and that must be stated, not assumed away.
  1953	+- **Staleness is intermittent by nature**, and it is the reason for the coordinator layer. A late result
  1954	+  applied to a moved-on board corrupts a game rarely and unreproducibly.
  1955	+- **The fallback can hide itself.** If the worker silently fails the game keeps working and simply plays
  1956	+  worse — hence one visible warning, and hence D2-A7 asserting ISMCTS rather than merely "a game happened".
  1957	+- **Seed drift between dev and prod** (D2-3) would be diagnosed as a search bug and is not one.
  1958	+- **D1's caveats stand**: the iteration budget was never strength-calibrated, and rollouts are ~117× the
  1959	+  tree cost.

  1975	+
  1976	+Production preview (`vite build` + `vite preview`, port 5310), Chromium via Playwright, Apple Silicon
  1977	+(darwin 25.5.0), default budget **200 iterations**, `rolloutCommandCap` 24, `rolloutApplyCap` 2048.
  1978	+Three complete games driven end to end; the numbers below are the second and third, where a patched
  1979	+`Worker` constructor recorded every message.
  1980	+
  1981	+| Quantity | Result |
  1982	+|---|---|
  1983	+| Worker asset actually served | `GET /assets/worker-DkZKnaJU.js → 200` (hashed production chunk, 52.8 kB) |
  1984	+| Searches posted / results received / worker errors | **33 / 33 / 0**, then **34 / 34 / 0** |
  1985	+| Worker round trip | **p50 152 ms, p95 240 ms, max 288 ms** |
  1986	+| Main-thread `longtask` entries during those searches | **0** (any reported entry would be ≥ 50 ms) |
  1987	+| Maximum `requestAnimationFrame` gap | **22 ms**, then **19 ms** |
  1988	+| Input delay, real trusted clicks (Event Timing, n = 12) | **0–1 ms** (`processingStart − startTime`) |
  1989	+| Search request serialized size | median **14.2 kB**, max 15.4 kB |

  1991	+| Fallback warnings logged | **none** |
  1992	+
  1993	+**Reading the numbers.** The frame gap is the load-bearing one: a 200-iteration search on the main thread
  1994	+would have shown a rAF gap of at least its own duration, so a max gap of 19–22 ms across whole games is
  1995	+direct evidence the search never ran there. Zero `longtask` entries says the same thing from the other side.
  1996	+
  1997	+The *first* pass at input delay used synthetic `.click()` and reported a flat 0 ms — worthless, because a
  1998	+programmatic click dispatches synchronously and measures nothing. The table's figure is from real Playwright
  1999	+input observed through `PerformanceEventTiming`.
  2000	+
  2001	+**D2-2 resolved.** Leaving `defs` in the per-request view costs 14.2 kB and **0.20 ms** of main-thread
  2002	+posting. Revision 1 called this "negligible" without measuring; measured, it is in fact negligible, and
  2003	+`Omit<PlayerView,'defs'>` stays unnecessary.
  2004	+
  2005	+**D2-6 / D2-A7 asserted positively.** Every AI decision in both instrumented games was a completed worker
  2006	+round trip (33/33, 34/34, zero errors, zero fallback warnings). This is the assertion the spec asked for —
  2007	+not "no warning appeared", which is only evidence of silence.
  2008	+
  2009	+**D2-A6: the budget does not need reducing.** Round trips of p50 152 ms / p95 240 ms bracket D1's headless
  2010	+~254 ms per decision, so the browser affords the **same 200 iterations D1 measured**. The risk the spec
  2011	+raised — that the human would face a weaker opponent than the 90.0 % one — did not materialise: the browser
  2012	+opponent is the D1 opponent. The budget still has not been *strength*-calibrated (D1's caveat stands); what
  2013	+is now known is that the browser is not the thing forcing it down.

  2105	     3	## BLOCKER
  2106	     4	
  2107	     5	**Staleness is tested at the wrong boundary; `respond()` cannot prove that React drops stale results.**
  2108	     6	
  2109	     7	`respond(init, request)` is pure and synchronous, so it has no knowledge of the outstanding request or current game state (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.md:19`). Yet D2-A4 proposes testing staleness by driving `respond` out of order (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.md:35`). The vulnerable operation is `commit`, which unconditionally replaces `stateRef.current` and appends logs (`apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:253`). A reply can race:
  2110	     8	
  2111	     9	- `restart()` replacing `stateRef.current` before React runs effect cleanup (`apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:274`).
  2112	    10	- Any human `choose()` that commits another state (`apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:262`); notably, concede remains legal even when the human is not acting (`packages/engine/src/legal.ts:19`).
  2113	    11	- StrictMode’s effect setup/cleanup/setup cycle (`apps/web/src/main.tsx:8`, `apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:285`).
  2114	    12	- Unmount, after which the callback must not call `commit`.
  2115	    13	
  2116	    14	**Fix:** The minimum acceptance rule is:
  2117	    15	
  2118	    16	```ts
  2119	    17	mounted &&
  2120	    18	activeRequestId === result.requestId &&
  2121	    19	stateRef.current === requestedState &&
  2122	    20	actingPlayer(requestedState) === AI
  2123	    21	```
  2124	    22	
  2125	    23	Then clear the active request before applying, re-check the command against `legalCommands(requestedState, AI)`, and commit from that same state. Every restart, external commit, effect cleanup, and unmount must synchronously invalidate the active ID; unmount must also terminate the worker. Test the main-thread receiver/controller with deferred replies after restart, human commit, StrictMode cleanup, and unmount. Keep `respond` testing only deterministic translation.
  2126	    24	
  2127	    25	**Search seeds must be stable per game position, not consumed per effect/request attempt.**
  2128	    26	
  2129	    27	The protocol carries a seed but never defines its allocation (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.md:17`). The synchronous agent currently advances its RNG once per actual decision (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/agent.ts:64`). A naïve worker port that advances a ref when the effect posts will consume an extra seed during StrictMode, retries, stale requests, or worker replacement (`apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:285`). Development and production can therefore choose different moves from the same game.
  2130	    28	
  2131	    29	**Fix:** Derive the search seed from `(gameSeed, committedAiDecisionIndex)`, or cache one seed against the captured state generation. Increment the decision index only when an AI command successfully commits; retries of the same position must resend the same seed. Do not derive it from `requestId`.

  2133	    31	## MAJOR
  2134	    32	
  2135	    33	**The Vite worker form and raw workspace TypeScript are sound, but production worker bundling is not an acceptance gate.**
  2136	    34	
  2137	    35	`new Worker(new URL('./worker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })` is Vite’s supported static form, and Vite emits it as a separate production chunk. Linked monorepo packages are treated as source when they export ESM, which these do (`packages/ai/package.json:5`, `packages/engine/package.json:5`). `server.fs.allow: ['../..']` correctly covers them in development (`apps/web/vite.config.ts:4`), but that option is dev-only; production uses the separate bundler path. See the [Vite worker documentation](https://vite.dev/guide/features#web-workers), [linked-dependency behavior](https://vite.dev/guide/dep-pre-bundling.html#monorepos-and-linked-dependencies), and [`server.fs.allow`](https://vite.dev/config/server-options.html#server-fs-allow).
  2138	    36	
  2139	    37	The divergence hazard is therefore not a known incompatibility—it is that D2-A7 runs tests/typecheck/lint but no web build (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.md:40`). A dev probe cannot catch production chunk generation, hashed asset loading, or deployment MIME/base-path failures.
  2140	    38	
  2141	    39	**Fix:** Add `pnpm --filter @fftcg/web build` and a production-preview browser test. It must load the emitted worker asset, complete at least one real request through `postMessage`, assert the ISMCTS log/status rather than fallback, and ideally finish D2-A1’s game. Keep `respond` unit tests, but do not call them a worker-boundary test.
  2142	    40	
  2143	    41	**`GreedyAgent` is the correct fallback; D2-6 does not yet detect every failure it claims to survive.**
  2144	    42	
  2145	    43	Running reduced ISMCTS on the main thread still invokes a pure synchronous search (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/search.ts:467`) whose rollout cost is variable and only work-capped (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/search.ts:53`). That would weaken the central non-blocking guarantee. Greedy is already the browser-safe, sub-millisecond path (`apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:11`, `apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:235`).
  2146	    44

  2148	    46

  2154	    52	
  2155	    53	**Fix:** Install listeners before init, catch construction/posting, handle `error`, `messageerror`, and typed errors, plus a generous per-request/startup watchdog.   5397	docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-26-heuristic-ai-design.md:38:- **A4**: the built signature is `preferredPayment(state, player, card)` — it operates on a full (determinised) `GameState`, not a bare `PlayerView`, because it needs backup/hand card definitions and `canPay`/`generateCp` from the engine. It also resolves multi-element costs via `requiredElements(def)` (§11.2.1.1 Light/Dark exemption, C3) and bounded backtracking over the required elements (C2, final fix wave) — not simply "dull backups then discard" in element order, and not a single scarcity-first greedy pass either: a single pass, even scarcest-element-first, can still strand a later element when the cheapest per-element pick spends a source only that element's rescue depended on (Codex's 3-element counterexample). Backtracking explores every source-to-element assignment and keeps the cheapest complete one.

  7123	## HIGH
  7124	
  7125	**A rejected or throwing delivery permanently stalls the AI and can also skip a seed.**
  7126	
  7127	`SearchCoordinator` clears `delivery`, advances `decisionIndex`, and calls the handler, but a `false` return only rolls the index back; it schedules no retry or fallback (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:357`, `apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:364`). `aiHandlers` returns `false` for an illegal worker command without changing state (`apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:266`), so the state-keyed effect never reruns (`apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:375`). If `produce()` or `onCommand()` throws, even the rollback is skipped. This is exactly the permanent spinner/no-state-change hang the repaired failure funnel was meant to eliminate.
  7128	
  7129	**Fix:** Treat rejection as a worker failure and schedule Greedy for the same target. Wrap production and delivery in `try/finally`, always restore the provisional index on failure, and provide a last-resort legal-command policy if Greedy itself rejects or throws.
  7130	
  7131	**A synchronous transport callback still enters fallback with no recovery target and returns without scheduling anything.**
  7132	
  7133	Handlers are exposed during construction and posting, but `active` is not assigned until after both posts return (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:193`, `apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:207`, `apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:242`). If an injected transport synchronously invokes `failure()` or sends a typed error, `fail()` finds no target, active request, or delivery and returns at `apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:324`. `request()` then sees `fallback` and returns without arming a watchdog (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:228`). Native Worker events are asynchronous, but the transport contract does not require that—and the comment explicitly anticipates synchronous failure.
  7134	
  7135	**Fix:** Establish a pending target before creating/exposing the transport and before posting. Let `fail()` recover from that target, and check for fallback immediately after factory return. Alternatively, explicitly require asynchronous callbacks in `SearchTransportFactory` and enforce that in adapters/tests.
  7136	
  7137	## MEDIUM
  7138	
  7139	**The seed transaction is not order-independent when a rejecting handler re-enters the coordinator.**
  7140	
  7141	The provisional increment lets a successful handler synchronously request the next position with seed N+1 (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:362`). But if that reentrant handler requests and then returns `false`, the new request was posted with N+1 before the counter rolls back to N (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:365`). If that request commits, the following position reuses N+1. Normal React delivery does not re-enter synchronously, so ordinary production commits are sound; the coordinator’s stated generality is not.
  7142	
  7143	**Fix:** Queue requests made during `onCommand` until its outcome is known, then release them using the committed index. Do not expose a provisional seed through `request()`.
  7144	
  7145	**Exactly one fallback warning is not guaranteed when failure arrives with nothing currently recoverable.**
  7146	
  7147	An idle failure sets permanent fallback but returns without warning when there is no active request or delivery (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:319`, `apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:324`). The test explicitly blesses deferral until another request (`apps/web/test/search-coordinator.test.ts:553`). If the preceding AI move ended the game, or the human concedes before another AI decision, that request never occurs and the visible warning count remains zero.
  7148	
  7149	**Fix:** Give the coordinator a game-lifetime warning sink instead of storing `onWarning` only on per-request targets. Ignore failures only after `dispose()`; otherwise log the first failure immediately.
  7150	
  7151	**The hook’s “mounted” condition depends on passive cleanup rather than synchronous unmount invalidation.**
  7152	
  7153	The coordinator’s disposed check is sound once `dispose()` runs (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:271`), but the hook invokes it from a passive `useEffect` cleanup (`apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:383`). The tests call `dispose()` directly and explicitly exclude React scheduling (`apps/web/test/useGame.test.ts:708`). A queued worker result can therefore be processed after DOM removal but before passive cleanup; a slow result can even schedule a zero-delay delivery.
  7154	
  7155	**Fix:** Dispose from a `useLayoutEffect` cleanup, and add a mounted React test that delivers a result during unmount rather than testing only the coordinator directly.
  7156	
  7157	**The measurement supports “no search-sized stall was observed,” not “the main thread was never blocked,” and “bracket” is numerically wrong.**
  7158	
  7159	Zero Long Task entries only rules out observed tasks at least 50 ms, while the 19–22 ms rAF gaps bound visible stalls in those two runs (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.md:115`). Given that this search is synchronous and round trips took 152–288 ms, the rAF result is good evidence that search itself did not execute on the main thread during the sample (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.md:122`). It does not prove zero blocking. Also, p50 152 ms and p95 240 ms are both below 254 ms, so they do not “bracket” D1’s figure (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.md:114`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.md:138`); only the 288 ms maximum crosses it.
  7160	
  7161	**Fix:** Say: “Across 67 observed searches, no ≥50 ms main-thread task occurred, max rAF gap was 22 ms, and no search-duration main-thread stall was observed.” Replace “bracket” with “were below, with a 288 ms maximum.”
  7162	
  7163	**The positive “every AI decision came from a worker result” assertion lacks commit correlation.**
  7164	
  7165	The acceptance protocol requires marking commits (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.md:59`), but the table reports only posts and received results (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.md:113`) before asserting every decision was a completed worker round trip (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.md:134`). A stale or rejected result still counts as received. No measurement harness or raw observations are committed; the web package has no browser-measurement script (`apps/web/package.json:6`). Also, 14.2 kB is the whole request, not the incremental size of `defs`, despite the attribution at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.md:130`.
  7166	
  7167	**Fix:** Record `requestId → accepted result → committed command`, report all three counts, and commit the production-preview harness plus raw summary. Label 14.2 kB as total request size, or measure with/without `defs`.
  7168	
  7169	## LOW
  7170	
  7171	**The startup watchdog becomes the short watchdog after supersession, not after proof that the worker started.**
  7172	
  7173	`starting` means only “transport did not exist before this request” (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:189`). If StrictMode or another cleanup supersedes the first request before any response, the replacement receives the 5-second watchdog even though the module may still be fetching/evaluating (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:234`). The test switches to the short watchdog only after a result, so it misses this distinction (`apps/web/test/search-coordinator.test.ts:520`).
  7174	
  7175	**Fix:** Track `ready` after the first valid worker response or add an init acknowledgement; use the startup deadline until then.
  7176	
  7177	**The fallback tests do not prove D2-A5’s “still finishes a game” condition.**
  7178	
  7179	Most failure tests assert one warning and one delivered command (`apps/web/test/search-coordinator.test.ts:164`). The hook-level fallback test stops after a handful of commits rather than reaching `state.result` (`apps/web/test/useGame.test.ts:835`). Its coordinator harness also accepts every command without updating live state and checks only command type, not structural legality (`apps/web/test/search-coordinator.test.ts:132`, `apps/web/test/search-coordinator.test.ts:174`).
  7180	
  7181	**Fix:** Drive one complete game for each failure class, using the production legality check and updating `readState` on every accepted command.
  7182	
  7183	**A stale illegal human event can cancel the only AI request before legality is established.**
  7184	
  7185	`choose()` invalidates first and checks whether the captured choice is still legal afterward (`apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:344`). A stale non-concede event that lands during AI control cancels the search, throws, leaves state unchanged, and gives the effect no reason to request again. The intended off-turn concede path is legal and safe.
  7186	
  7187	**Fix:** Check legality first, then invalidate immediately before `apply`; there is no asynchronous gap between those operations.
  7188	
  7189	**The actual asynchronous result/error/watchdog/state-change matrix is otherwise single-delivery and state-safe.**
  7190	
  7191	A winning result clears active and cancels its watchdog before scheduling (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:293`); a later failure cancels and replaces that delivery (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:319`); a winning failure invalidates everything and guards its fallback (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:310`); state change, restart, cleanup, and concede cancel both states (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:250`); delivery rechecks identity and actor (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:359`). Thus, after excluding the synchronous-callback and rejected-delivery holes above, I found no ordering that double-commits or applies a command to a different state.
  7192	
  7193	**Fix:** Preserve these checks and add permutation tests for result→error, error→result, result/watchdog at the same deadline, and accepted-result→concede.
  7194	
  7195	## WHAT I WOULD DO DIFFERENTLY
  7196	
  7197	**Make the coordinator an explicit transactional state machine.**
  7198	
  7199	The current `active`/`delivery`/`fallback` combination encodes states indirectly, which created both liveness holes.
  7200	
  7201	**Fix:** Model `idle | posting | searching | delivering | fallback | disposed`, with one decision token owning the target, seed, watchdog, and exactly one terminal outcome: committed, superseded, or recovered.
  7202	
  7203	**Design C3 deck choices as private/revealed information, not raw target IDs.**
  7204	
  7205	`Pending.chooseTargets` stores live `CardId`s (`packages/engine/src/state.ts:36`), `viewFor` copies pending wholesale (`packages/engine/src/view.ts:33`), and determinisation copies those IDs after minting replacements for hidden cards (`packages/engine/src/determinise.ts:41`, `packages/engine/src/determinise.ts:51`). Reeve’s private “look” also invalidates the search’s current assumption that every action becomes public (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/search.ts:372`).
  7206	
  7207	**Fix:** Define authorized candidate visibility and stable card references before adding deck selection. Rebind candidates in determinisations, redact them from unauthorized views, and decide how private opponent actions are keyed without leaking them into root observations. The D2 protocol can continue carrying `PlayerView`; it does not need a separate deck-search message.
  7208	
  7209	**Split Cloud’s Attack-Phase entry and add source-aware return protection before implementing the clause.**
  7210	
  7211	Main1 currently jumps atomically to attack declaration (`packages/engine/src/phases.ts:50`), while `enterAttackDeclaration` emits preparation and declaration together (`packages/engine/src/resolve.ts:389`). The only flag is `cannotBeBroken` (`packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:75`), and `toHand` carries no cause/controller transition (`packages/engine/src/resolve.ts:166`).
  7212	
  7213	**Fix:** Enter Attack Phase preparation first, enqueue beginning-phase triggers, then continue into declaration. Add a source-aware field→hand transition and an opponent-Summon/ability return-protection flag.
  7214	
  7215	**Trim only the test-facing fallback seed bookkeeping, not the coordinator layer itself.**
  7216	
  7217	Fallback is permanent (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:145`) and Greedy uses its own stateful RNG (`apps/web/src/game/search/coordinator.ts:342`), so advancing/exposing the worker’s next search seed after fallback has no behavioral consumer; the test at `apps/web/test/search-coordinator.test.ts:597` proves an inert value.
  7218	
  7219	**Fix:** Stop asserting search-seed advancement under permanent fallback, and rerun the browser timing measurement after C3 changes branching and request visibility.

    61	  if (!inst) throw new Error(`unknown card id ${id}`)

    81	 * Zone by the §12.4.4 zero-power rule process instead.

    84	  return Math.max(0, (def.power ?? 0) + card.powerBonus)

    88	  return effectivePower(defOf(state, card.id), card)

    92	  return new Set([...defOf(state, card.id).keywords, ...card.granted])

    96	  const players: [PlayerState, PlayerState] = [state.players[0], state.players[1]]
    97	  players[p] = f(state.players[p])
    98	  return { ...state, players }

   351	export function decodeAction(view: PlayerView, key: ActionKey): Command | null {
   352	  const parts = key.split(FIELD)
   353	  const decoder = (DECODERS as Record<string, Decoder | undefined>)[parts[0] ?? '']

   358	  // payment discards another copy of the card being cast would otherwise decode both to the same id and be
   359	  // rejected as "cannot discard the card you are casting". Decoding in field order hands out distinct copies.

   361	  const take = (ref: CardRef): CardId | null => {
   362	    const n = taken.get(ref) ?? 0
   363	    const v = idx.byRef.get(ref)?.[n]
   364	    if (v === undefined) return null
   365	    taken.set(ref, n + 1)

   367	  }

   373	    ids: (field) => {

    13	 * The ability executor (spec C1-3). No card-specific code lives here: this is an interpreter for the `Effect`
    14	 * AST in abilities.ts, and `packages/cards` writes the ASTs.
    15	 *
    16	 * LAYERING — this module imports nothing from `rules.ts`, `phases.ts` or `apply.ts`, because `rules.ts` imports
    17	 * `enqueueTrigger` from here (spec C1-8 wants zone transitions to enqueue their own triggers at the moment of
    18	 * removal). Interleaving resolution with rule processes is therefore the outer reducer's job: `settle` in
    19	 * `apply.ts` alternates `runRuleProcesses` and `drainResolution` until both are quiet.
    20	 *
    21	 * MVP0-SIMPLIFICATION (spec C1-4): there is no stack and no response window. A triggered clause resolves
    22	 * immediately, in trigger order, and the opponent cannot answer it.
    23	 *
    24	 * C1's atomicity rule is REFINED by spec C2-6, not replaced: a frame is atomic WITHIN itself, across every
    25	 * prompt it raises; rule processes run BETWEEN frames. `drainResolution` therefore completes exactly one frame
    26	 * and yields while queued work remains, so `settle` gets its §12.3 pass in before the next frame starts.
    27	 * Without that yield, Luso's "break it" resolved BEFORE §12.4.5 had broken the Forward its own damage killed —

    35	/** Push a triggered clause onto the agenda. The frame starts at path `[]` — the top of `ability.effects`. */
    36	export function enqueueTrigger(state: GameState, source: CardId, controller: PlayerId, ability: Ability, triggerEvent: TriggerEvent | null = null): GameState {
    37	  const frame: Frame = { abilityId: ability.id, source, controller, path: [], chosen: [], modes: [], triggerEvent }
    38	  return { ...state, resolution: { ...state.resolution, queue: [...state.resolution.queue, frame] } }
    39	}

    41	/**
    42	 * One card dealing one lot of damage to one recipient — the SINGLE record combat damage (`attack.ts`) and the
    43	 * ability `damage` effect both produce, because the printed text says "deals damage", not "deals combat
    44	 * damage" (spec C2-7). Exactly one of `target`/`victim` is non-null.
    45	 *
    46	 * `sourceController` is passed in rather than derived: the source may be about to leave the field, and party
    47	 * attribution is by MEMBERSHIP, not array position (spec C2-8).
    48	 */
    49	export interface DamageOccurrence {
    50	  readonly source: CardId
    51	  readonly sourceController: PlayerId
    52	  readonly target: CardId | null
    53	  readonly victim: PlayerId | null
    54	  readonly amount: number
    55	}

    57	/**
    58	 * Queue the `dealtDamage` clauses of every damage source in `hits`, in hit order. Damage inside one batch is
    59	 * simultaneous (§10.1.4.2), so callers apply ALL of it first and dispatch once — a source that is about to be
    60	 * broken by the same batch still triggers, exactly as a zone-change watcher does (spec C2-4).
    61	 */
    62	export function enqueueDamageTriggers(state: GameState, hits: readonly DamageOccurrence[]): GameState {
    63	  let s = state
    64	  for (const h of hits) {
    65	    if (h.target === null && h.victim === null) continue
    66	    const to = h.target !== null ? 'forward' : 'player'
    67	    const code = state.cards[h.source]?.code
    68	    const event: TriggerEvent = { kind: 'damage', source: h.source, sourceController: h.sourceController, target: h.target, victim: h.victim, amount: h.amount }
    69	    for (const a of (code === undefined ? undefined : state.defs[code])?.abilities ?? []) {
    70	      if (a.trigger.kind !== 'dealtDamage' || a.trigger.to !== to) continue
    71	      // "deals damage to YOUR OPPONENT" (Luso, Prishe) is a real restriction, not decoration. It held only
    72	      // because today's single producer always damages the opponent; encoding it here means a future
    73	      // self-damage or redirect path cannot silently fire these on their own controller.
    74	      if (!damagedSideMatches(state, a.trigger.whose, h)) continue
    75	      s = enqueueTrigger(s, h.source, h.sourceController, a, event)
    76	    }
    77	  }
    78	  return s
    79	}

    82	/**
    83	 * Is the damaged side the one the clause names, relative to the SOURCE's controller (spec C2-10)?
    84	 * For damage to a Forward the side is that Forward's controller, looked up while it is still on the field —
    85	 * the pool's only `to: 'forward'` clause is unrestricted (`whose: 'any'`), so this is guarded, not exercised.
    86	 */
    87	function damagedSideMatches(state: GameState, whose: TriggerWhose, h: DamageOccurrence): boolean {
    88	  if (whose === 'any') return true
    89	  const damaged = h.victim !== null ? h.victim : h.target === null ? null : findFieldCard(state, h.target)?.owner ?? null
    90	  if (damaged === null) return true   // nothing attributable to compare against
    91	  return whose === 'self' ? damaged === h.sourceController : damaged === opponentOf(h.sourceController)
    92	}

    94	/** The clause a frame is executing, or null if the def no longer declares it (a hot-swapped card pool). */
    95	export function abilityOf(state: GameState, frame: Frame): Ability | null {
    96	  const code = state.cards[frame.source]?.code
    97	  const def = code === undefined ? undefined : state.defs[code]
    98	  return def?.abilities?.find((a) => a.id === frame.abilityId) ?? null
    99	}

   102	// Targeting

   104	
   105	function defFor(state: GameState, id: CardId) {
   106	  const code = state.cards[id]?.code
   107	  return code === undefined ? undefined : state.defs[code]
   108	}
   109	
   110	function matchesFilter(state: GameState, source: CardId, id: CardId, filter: TargetFilter | undefined): boolean {
   111	  if (!filter) return true
   112	  const def = defFor(state, id)
   113	  if (!def) return false
   114	  if (filter.type !== undefined && def.type !== filter.type) return false
   115	  // "Character" is Forward, Backup OR Monster and never Summon (§7.2), which a single `type` cannot say — both
   116	  // Prishe's and Luso's Break-Zone retrievals need it (spec C2-9). `type` and `types` conjoin: a filter carrying
   117	  // both must satisfy both.
   118	  if (filter.types !== undefined && !filter.types.includes(def.type)) return false
   119	  if (filter.element !== undefined && !def.elements.includes(filter.element)) return false
   120	  if (filter.maxCost !== undefined && def.cost > filter.maxCost) return false
   121	  if (filter.excludeSource && id === source) return false
   122	  if (filter.excludeSourceName) {
   123	    const src = defFor(state, source)
   124	    if (src && src.name === def.name) return false
   125	  }
   126	  return true
   127	}

   129	/**
   130	 * The legal targets of one `TargetSpec`, in a fixed player-0-then-1 order so a live state and its
   131	 * determinisation enumerate the same candidates in the same order (spec C1-A6).
   132	 */
   133	export function targetCandidates(state: GameState, source: CardId, controller: PlayerId, spec: TargetSpec): CardId[] {
   134	  const owners: readonly PlayerId[] = spec.controller === 'any' ? [0, 1]
   135	    : spec.controller === 'self' ? [controller] : [opponentOf(controller)]
   136	  const out: CardId[] = []
   137	  for (const p of ([0, 1] as const).filter((q) => owners.includes(q))) {
   138	    const ps = state.players[p]
   139	    const ids = spec.zone === 'breakZone' ? ps.breakZone
   140	      : (spec.zone === 'forwards' ? ps.forwards : ps.backups).map((c) => c.id)
   141	    for (const id of ids) if (matchesFilter(state, source, id, spec.filter)) out.push(id)
   142	  }
   143	  return out
   144	}

   150	function setFieldCard(state: GameState, id: CardId, f: (c: FieldCard) => FieldCard): GameState {
   151	  const loc = findFieldCard(state, id)
   152	  if (!loc) return state
   153	  return updatePlayer(state, loc.owner, (ps) => (loc.zone === 'forwards'
   154	    ? { ...ps, forwards: ps.forwards.map((c) => (c.id === id ? f(c) : c)) }
   155	    : { ...ps, backups: ps.backups.map((c) => (c.id === id ? f(c) : c))}))
   156	}
   157	
   158	function removeFromField(state: GameState, id: CardId): GameState {
   159	  const loc = findFieldCard(state, id)
   160	  if (!loc) return state
   161	  return updatePlayer(state, loc.owner, (ps) => (loc.zone === 'forwards'
   162	    ? { ...ps, forwards: ps.forwards.filter((c) => c.id !== id) }
   163	    : { ...ps, backups: ps.backups.filter((c) => c.id !== id) }))
   164	}
   165	
   166	/** §7.10: a card always goes to its OWNER's zone, not its controller's. Returns null if the card is nowhere movable. */
   167	function toHand(state: GameState, id: CardId): GameState | null {
   168	  const owner = state.cards[id]?.owner
   169	  if (owner === undefined) return null
   170	  let s = state
   171	  if (findFieldCard(state, id)) s = removeFromField(s, id)
   172	  else {
   173	    const holder = ([0, 1] as const).find((p) => state.players[p].breakZone.includes(id))
   174	    if (holder === undefined) return null
   175	    s = updatePlayer(s, holder, (ps) => ({ ...ps, breakZone: ps.breakZone.filter((x) => x !== id) }))
   176	  }
   177	  return updatePlayer(s, owner, (ps) => ({ ...ps, hand: [...ps.hand, id] }))
   178	}

   366	interface FrameResult { state: GameState; events: Event[]; pending: Pending | null; frame: Frame; steps: number }
   367	
   368	function runFrame(state: GameState, frame: Frame): FrameResult {
   369	  const ability = abilityOf(state, frame)
   370	  const base: FrameResult = { state, events: [], pending: null, frame, steps: state.resolution.steps }
   371	  if (!ability) return base   // the clause vanished with its def; drop the frame rather than throw
   372	  const ctx: Ctx = {
   373	    state, events: [], source: frame.source, controller: frame.controller, abilityId: frame.abilityId,
   374	    path: [...frame.path], chosen: [...frame.chosen], modes: [...frame.modes],
   375	    triggerEvent: frame.triggerEvent,
   376	    resume: frame.path, suspend: null, steps: state.resolution.steps,
   377	  }
   378	  runEffects(ctx, ability.effects, 0, frame.path.length > 0)
   379	  return {
   380	    state: ctx.state, events: ctx.events, pending: ctx.suspend, steps: ctx.steps,
   381	    frame: { ...frame, path: ctx.path, chosen: ctx.chosen, modes: ctx.modes },
   382	  }
   383	}
